decisions.reason: As a core safety shoe line, it builds directly on the firm's strongest footwear knowledge and in-house development capabilities, so management is likely to retain and refine it.

The comfort insole is closely related to the existing footwear business and can be improved through the firm's product-development know-how, though as a complementary item it is somewhat easier to discontinue than core shoes.
The supportive insole fits the firm's established expertise in work-footwear function and user needs, making it a product the firm can learn from and develop further rather than remove quickly.
An ergonomic safety shoe series is highly aligned with the firm's core capabilities and its dedicated web presence suggests a stronger strategic commitment, making withdrawal unlikely.
Firefighter and rescue boots remain within the firm's protective-footwear competence base, but the more specialized segment gives slightly more risk than mainstream safety shoes.
The moulded insole is closely connected to the firm's existing shoe platform and its prominent placement indicates active commercial support, so management would likely keep it on the market.
